value: D.1.1 Two teams tied on points: result(s) of the game(s) between the two teams.
D.1.2 If points and goal average in the games between the two teams are still equal: goal average of all games played in the group by each team.
D.1.3 More than two teams tied: second classification using only the results of games between the tied teams.
D.1.4 Still tied after the second classification: goal average in the games between the teams still tied.
D.1.5 Still tied: goal average from all their games in the group.
D.1.6 If a multi-team tie is reduced to two teams at any stage: apply D.1.1 and D.1.2.
D.1.7 If still more than two teams tied at any stage: repeat from D.1.3.
D.1.8 Goal average is always calculated by division (points scored / points allowed).
tiebreak.source: FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2004, Appendix D (Classification of teams), D.1-D.1.8, as reproduced at https://www.luxembourg.basketball/calcul-du-classement-extrait-des-regles-fiba-2004/
tiebreak.note: Wikipedia's 2006 group tables state the same order ("1) points; 2) head-to-head points; 3) head-to-head goal average; 4) head-to-head number of points scored") and use goal average (GAvg) in a three-way tie note; Wikipedia's 4th step (head-to-head points scored) does not appear in the 2004 rule text, which falls back to goal average in all group games. The 2004 rule text is used here.

research.no_hindsight_policy: This file records the event's format, calendar, teams and registered rosters only. No score, result, standing, award, attendance or statistic of the 2006 event is recorded. Knockout games carry bracket slots, not teams. Round-of-16 group-position slots were derived from the real pairings at each time slot; only the slot labels are stored.
conflicts: Uniform numbers: Wikipedia squads page differs from FIBA for Lebanon (Bassem Balaa W#10/F#14, Roy Samaha W#14/F#10), Italy (Fabio Di Bella W#4/F#13, Marco Belinelli W#9/F#4, Marco Mordente W#13/F#9) and Senegal (Sitapha Savane W#8/F#12, Moustapha Niang W#12/F#8). FIBA numbers used.

Wikipedia squads page "Team" column is in several cases the club signed for 2006-07 (e.g. Shane Battier Houston, Rasho Nesterovic Toronto, Carlos Arroyo Orlando, Walter Herrmann Charlotte, Mickael Gelabale Seattle); it is kept as club_listed_at_tournament and not used as the 2005-06 club.
Senegal #11: Wikipedia names "Souleymane Aw"; FIBA registers "Jules Richard Aw" (born 1986-12-25). The linked Wikipedia article (born 1999) is a different person.
Senegal #6: Wikipedia "Pape Ibrahim Faye" (born 1980 per squads page) vs FIBA "Cheikh 'Pif' Faye" born 1987-05-19. FIBA used.

Senegal #10 Mamadou Diouf: Wikipedia year 1983 vs FIBA 1977-08-17; Senegal #12 Moustapha Niang: Wikipedia year 1977 vs FIBA 1983-11-10; Senegal #4 Makhtar Ndiaye: Wikipedia 1972 vs FIBA 1973-12-12. FIBA used.

Venezuela #6: Wikipedia "Ernesto Mijares", FIBA "Yumerving Mijares". Venezuela #8 Tomas Aguilera and Panama #11 Michael Hicks: linked Wikipedia articles describe different people (birth years 1988, 1983); FIBA birth dates used and those articles ignored.
Italy: FIBA history birth date for Marco Belinelli (1986-03-25) agrees with basketball-reference; Fabio Di Bella 1978-12-13 (FIBA only), Marco Mordente FIBA 1979-01-07 = Wikipedia 1979-01-07.
China: Yi Jianlian (FIBA 1987-10-27; reports of 1984) and Wang Zhizhi (FIBA 1979-07-08; NBA/bbr 1977-07-08) age discrepancies.
Julius Nwosu: FIBA/Wikipedia 1971-01-05 vs bbr 1971-05-01. Peter John Ramos: FIBA/Wikipedia 1985-05-23 vs bbr 1985-05-13. bbr value recorded as unverified.
Tiebreak: Wikipedia lists head-to-head points scored as a 4th criterion; the 2004 FIBA rule text uses goal average of all group games instead. Rule text used.
Turkey #5 is registered by FIBA as "Ermal Kurtoglu" (Wikipedia article title: Ermal Kuqo).
